note: Rows where the gate deliberately differs from hyperpolymath/ijson-jcs at the pinned commit (fixtures/oracle/ijson-jcs.json, 2c880594) and at main 1735d68. Owner ruling R3 (2026-11-17): a finite float whose RFC 8785 text is an integer token outside +-(2^53-1) is refused (UNSAFE_FLOAT_INTEGER), because ijson-jcs's own strict reader refuses that text, so canon output would not be valid input. ijson-jcs accepts and canonicalises these inputs. The divergence is proposed upstream in docs/proposals/STANDARDS-BUDGETS-FLOATS.adoc (pending standards); until it lands, these rows are reported as known divergences by tools/ijson-jcs-diff.mjs and pinned by test/json.test.js. The transcribed oracle file is left as the oracle's own behaviour.
budgetDivergencesNote: Second divergence class (proposal J-3): value budgets that ijson-jcs does not have. Measured 2026-11-17 on binaries built at the pin 2c880594 and at main 1735d68: both print OK for these inputs; the gate refuses them. Rows are generated (tools/budget-divergence-rows.mjs), one step over the limit. Not probed here: the 256 MiB input budget (a file over 256 MiB), which is enforced at the CLI edge only. The depth budget (127) is NOT a divergence: it matches serde_json's text limit at the pin byte for byte.
